title: IPL Trades: Gujarat, Delhi Discuss Ashutosh Sharma Swap Ahead of Retention Deadline
excerpt: Cricbuzz reports Gujarat approached Delhi months ago for the Rs 3.8 crore finisher and Delhi may now revisit the offer — while a counter-report insists he is not up for trade at all.
body:
• Delhi Capitals finisher Ashutosh Sharma has emerged as a trade candidate ahead of the November 17 IPL retention and release deadline, Cricbuzz reports.
  • Gujarat Titans approached Delhi for the 28-year-old a couple of months ago and got no immediate response; Delhi, under a new coach and management, could now revisit the offer.
  • Delhi are understood to want a fast bowler in exchange; Lucknow Super Giants are the other possible destination named in the reports.
  • A conflicting report says people privy to Delhi's trade options insist Ashutosh is not up for trade — nothing is agreed, and neither franchise has confirmed a deal.

IPL trade activity is gathering pace ahead of the November 17 deadline for retentions and releases, and a new name has joined the market: Ashutosh Sharma, the Delhi Capitals finisher, is a potential trade candidate, most probably in exchange for a fast bowler, Cricbuzz reports.

The Shubman Gill-led Gujarat Titans approached Delhi for Ashutosh a couple of months ago, Cricbuzz confirms, but there was no immediate response from the Capitals. Delhi, under a new coach and management, could now revisit that offer. Which franchise Delhi would deal with, and which player would move the other way, is still not clear.

Why Gujarat want a finisher

Gujarat are seeking a finisher and are believed to be contemplating releasing Shahrukh Khan. Ashutosh fits the profile they are shopping for: he has built a record of finishing matches from precarious positions, first for Punjab Kings and then for Delhi. Gujarat have tried this route before — they approached another franchise a few months ago offering tearaway fast bowler Ashok Sharma in exchange for a finisher, and the offer was not considered. Lucknow Super Giants, who are understood to be looking to consolidate their batting, are the other possible destination named by CricTracker and Cricbuzz.

The counter-report

The talks are not uncontested. A trade tracker summary of the reporting notes that journalist Kushan Sarkar has reported the opposite — that Ashutosh is not up for trade, according to people privy to Delhi's trading options. That leaves the two accounts directly at odds with nine days left before the deadline, and as of November 8 neither Delhi nor Gujarat has officially confirmed any agreement.

What Ashutosh is worth

Delhi bought the 28-year-old right-hander for Rs 3.8 crore at the mega auction two years ago. Reports of his most recent season credit him with 171 runs in eight matches at a strike rate above 180 — the late-overs profile that makes finishers the scarcest currency in the trade window. If Delhi do deal, the return they want tells its own story: not cash, not a batter, but pace, the other scarce commodity, ahead of the IPL 2027 mini-auction.
